subject: Hosted API — topline commit ranges + peak TPS acceptance
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@wavepay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + numbers from our call — WavePay traffic profile

Thanks again for the demo today — helpful conversation. Quick recap from our side and a couple clarifying asks so you can price appropriately:

- Expected ramp: we currently see ~20M tokens/month (pilot). If things go well we expect a 3–6 month ramp to ~160M tokens/month (we're modeling mid-case ~100M).
- Typical request mix: ~70% chat/generation, 30% embeddings/short rewrites. Average prompt+response token per chat ~340 tokens.
- Traffic shape: steady baseline through week, with two predictable flash windows (campaigns) where TPS spikes for ~15–30 minutes. Peak observed in our simulations: ~1,100 TPS (in-staging). Sustained peak for planning should be ~400–600 TPS.
- Budget envelope: we have a target list price around $12–$18 per 1M tokens depending on commit and burst options. Our procurement team prefers committed-month slabs (3 month initial commitment, then quarterly review).

Asks from us: please confirm how you price the following and what the expected $/1M would be for each band — we need these to the procurement team tomorrow:
  1) Pay-as-you-go (no commitment) 
  2) 3-month committed band: 40–80M/mo, 80–140M/mo, 140M+ /mo
  3) Burst allowance: can we get an explicit explanation of your burst model (bps/short bursts at x% above commit) and whether you charge overage at pay-as-you-go rate or prorated?

I've attached the traffic profile we ran in staging (WavePay_Traffic_Profile_v1.xlsx). If you can send a rough estimate and a short sample invoice for the 100M/month mid-case that shows the target $/1M and monthly total that would be ideal.

Best,
Alyssa

Thanks Alyssa — great context and the traffic file helps a lot. TL;DR below and then a short table with pricing options. Karthik is our pricing lead; I've looped him to confirm commitment math and burst SLA.

Clarifying notes:
- We price tokens at generation+input token counts (so your 340 tokens/chat maps directly). Confirmed.
- Burst behavior: hosted API supports policy-based burst windows. Short bursts (<= 20 minutes) can exceed committed TPS if capacity available; overage billing depends on committed product: for pure PAYG overage = PAYG rate; for committed slabs we typically provide a burst buffer (percentage of commit) and then overage at a blended overage rate. Karthik will add precise bands below.

Pricing options (approximate — subject to formal quote):
1) PAYG (no commit): $27 / 1M tokens (good for pilots; no SLA).
2) 3-month commit slabs (month average over the 3 months):
   - 40–80M/mo: $18 / 1M tokens
   - 80–140M/mo: $13 / 1M tokens
   - 140M+ /mo: $10 / 1M tokens (requires 3mo commit + minimum monthly UPC)

Burst allowance example (illustrative):
- For the 80–140M slab we provide a 25% burst buffer (so if you commit 100M/month we allow short bursts up to 125M-equivalent tokens for the billing period before overage rates apply). Overage rate above burst buffer = PAYG * 0.9 (i.e., slightly discounted).

Sample mid-case math (100M/month at $13 /1M):
- Token cost = 100 * $13 = $1,300 / month
- If you hit a 1,100 TPS flash for 20 minutes (approx 1.32M tokens in that window if average token counts hold), that fits within a typical 25% burst buffer for a 100M commit.

Next steps I suggest:
- Karthik to confirm final band pricing & burst SLA language (within 24 hours).
- We'll send a short sample invoice for the 100M mid-case and a one-pager on burst policies and limits.
- Schedule a 30 minute follow-up with procurement + engineering to lock in commit and SLOs (we have availability Mon/Tue next week).

I'll send the sample invoice & brief doc shortly.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
